hypothesis:
The MLP bracket is closed and it says something about where to look next. 3x costs +0.006633 of capacity while 5x gains only -0.002872 -- removing width hurts 2.3x more than adding it helps, so 4x is a genuine interior optimum and capacity is strongly convex. Width cannot be bought or sold profitably in either direction. What that leaves is capacity-free structure: changes that improve how information moves through the stack without adding parameters or FLOPs.

This model injects the embedding x0 into every layer through x0_lambdas, but has no layer-to-layer skips. Every deep layer can see the raw token, and none can see what the corresponding shallow layer computed. U-net skips pair layer i with layer n-1-i: the first half pushes its input, the second half adds it back through a learned scalar. Six scalars for a 12-layer stack.

The specific reason to expect it here rather than generically: the attention placement work showed this model depends on periodic global integration and is badly hurt by long stretches where information cannot move -- clustering the full-context layers cost +0.0031 and dissolving them cost +0.0028. A skip is another route for information to cross depth, and it is the only one this architecture does not already have. x0 injection provides a shortcut from the input; nothing provides a shortcut from mid-stack.
change_summary:
Five coordinated edits. A new nn.Parameter skip_lambdas of length n_layer//2 = 6, zero-initialised so the model starts exactly at the champion; an explicit zero_() alongside the other scalar inits; a skip_params list, its own AdamW group matching x0's settings, and the extended completeness assert; and the forward loop, where the first half appends x to a stack and the second half pops its partner and adds it scaled.
The parameter-count assert in setup_optimizer is what makes this safe to attempt: a new parameter that is not grouped fails loudly at init rather than silently going untrained. I extended that assert rather than working around it. Compile mode also reverts to default, for the wall-clock reason established by t0434/t0435/t0436/t0438, at a known -0.00067 handicap.
expected_val_bpb_effect:
Zero-init means this cannot hurt through the mechanism itself at step 0; any harm arrives through optimisation or through throughput. The cost model says a full-width elementwise op per layer buys ~2.8% of steps, but this adds six adds across twelve layers, ~0.5 per layer, and under torch.compile the add sits immediately after the existing resid/x0 mul-add so it may fuse into that kernel and cost nothing. I therefore expect steps to fall by 0 to 1.5% beyond the 1.14% the compile revert forfeits, and I will read anything beyond that as the skips failing to fuse.
On the mechanism: -0.002 to +0.001. The handicap means raw must clear -0.0007 of mechanism to beat the champion, so a small win will read as a null and route to a re-buy with autotune rather than to closing the axis.
risk:
This is the most invasive edit of the session -- five coordinated changes across four regions of the file -- and its crash risk is correspondingly the highest. Three of the five are guarded by exact-string asserts, and the parameter-count assert catches the grouping error at init. What none of them catch is a semantic error in the pairing: skips is a stack, so pop() gives layer i its partner n-1-i, and if I have that backwards the model still runs and still trains, just wired to the wrong partner. I checked the arithmetic (i=6 pops the entry pushed at i=5, which is n-1-i for n=12) but a silently wrong pairing would look like a null result rather than a bug, and I would not be able to tell them apart from the score.
Second risk: zero-init makes the skip neutral at step 0, which is safe but also means a real effect needs the scalars to move meaningfully within 2800 steps. t0424 showed a learned scalar can simply return to its initialisation and produce an exact null -- and if that happens here, the honest reading is unresolved-below-floor, not 'skips do not help'.
